extracted.intended_audience: laboratory technicians, bacteriologists, and researchers performing serological assays and necropsies on experimental animals
extracted.subtask_description: Practical laboratory protocols for preparing and diluting sera, performing microscopical and macroscopical agglutination tests, opsonin and complement-fixation assays, and for conducting post-mortem examinations and preparing permanent museum specimens of experimental animals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dilution of serum using teat pipette
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare serial dilutions by using a Pasteur capillary pipette fitted with a rubber teat, making a grease-pencil mark as volume index, drawing successive equal volumes of saline separated by air indices, then aspirating one volume of serum and ejecting into saline to make defined percent dilutions (e.g., 10%, 1%, 0.1%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps 2–17: nick and cut pipette square; fit teat; mark ~2–3 cm from open end; compress teat to expel air; draw saline to mark and create air index; repeat to obtain nine equal volumes of saline, aspirate one volume of serum to make 10% solution; mix thoroughly by repeatedly drawing up and expelling the fluid. Further dilutions by same method. NOTE: "The saline diluting fluid must always be taken into the pipette first, otherwise... traces of serum added to the saline may entirely vitiate the subsequent observations"; avoid diluting more than one serum from same saline to prevent contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Wright's capillary method when serum yield is small
rubrics_metrics.description: When the yield of serum from the specimen is small and ordinary dilution is impracticable, carry out dilution by Wright's method in a capillary teat pipette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply teat-pipette dilution method described above (capillary volumes and air-indexing) instead of larger graduated pipettes when sample volume is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hanging-drop microscopical agglutination test setup and controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Make five hanging-drop preparations combining bouillon culture with pooled serum (control), undiluted specific serum (50%), and dilutions of specific serum (10%, 1%, 0.1%) mounted as specified and examined microscopically for agglutination/clumping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare: (a) control = culture + pooled serum; (b) 50% = culture + undiluted specific serum; (c) 5% = culture + 10% serum; (d) 0.5% = culture + 1% serum; (e) 0.05% = culture + 0.1% serum. Note time and examine control first to confirm motility and even distribution. Interpretations: positive = bacilli collected in large clumps (agglutination); concentrated serum may cause clumping from viscosity—distinguish by comparing to control and diluted preparations. If 5% shows no aggregation, wait up to 30 minutes before recording a negative. Use series of dilutions to compare potency/valency across sera.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macroscopical agglutination (sedimentation) reaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Mix defined volumes of bouillon culture with diluted sera (10, 1, 0.1% remaining ~90 c.mm.), fill sedimentation pipettes or teat pipettes, incubate vertically at 37°C for 1–2 hours and compare granular precipitate (positive) to uniform turbidity (negative) relative to pooled serum control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pipette 90 c.mm. of bouillon culture into each serum dilution tube and pooled serum tube; aspirate into sedimentation tubes or teat pipettes, seal lower ends, label with dilutions (5, 0.5, 0.05%), incubate vertically at 37°C for 1–2 hours; positive reaction shows granular precipitate, negative gives uniform turbidity like pooled serum control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of 'washed cells' for opsonin assay
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect blood into sodium citrate, centrifuge to separate, remove supernatant plasma, wash the red cells with normal saline repeatedly until leucocytes remain, then redistribute leucocytes evenly through red cell mass for use as 'washed cells'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: cleanse puncture site, collect blood into citrate solution, centrifuge to compact cells with leucocyte layer, remove supernatant, refill with normal saline and re-centrifuge twice, remove supernatant nearly down to leucocyte level, rotate tube to distribute leucocytes evenly through red cells; set tube upright in plasticine block for assay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of bacterial emulsion for opsonin assay
rubrics_metrics.description: Emulsify surface growth of 18–24 hour culture in saline, allow large masses to settle, centrifuge and examine supernatant opalescent emulsion microscopically to ensure freedom from clumps; if clumped, reprepare by scraping and grinding in an agate mortar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsatisfactory due to clumps, scrape growth, grind with successive small quantities of saline in an agate mortar until even; place tube next to washed cells in preparation block; aim for homogenous opalescent suspension free of clumps for reliable opsonin results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opsonin estimation and calculation of opsonic index
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare capillary pipettes containing equal volumes of washed cells, bacterial emulsion and either specific serum or pooled serum (control); incubate, spread films from incubated mixtures, fix and stain, count bacteria ingested by first 50 consecutive polymorphonuclear leucocytes to compute phagocytic index and opsonic index (specific/control ×100).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aspirate one volume washed cells, air index, one volume bacterial emulsion, air index, one volume specific serum; mix thoroughly on a 3×1 slide, seal pipette tip, incubate (set clock 15 minutes), at end mix and divide specimen between slides, make blood films covering half slide, fix and stain under comparable conditions, examine with 1/12 inch oil immersion, count bacteria in first 50 polymorphonuclears for both specific and control preparations. Phagocytic index = average bacteria per leucocyte; opsonic index = (specific numerator ÷ control denominator) ×100.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixing and staining consistency for opsonin films
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix and stain films under strictly comparable conditions using a staining rack and troughs; Leishman's stain recommended for routine work (except tubercle bacilli), with specified fixation and staining times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place slides in alcoholic Leishman's stain for two minutes to fix, transfer to diluted stain for ten minutes, then wash in distilled water until clear and dry. Note: films with tubercle bacilli require Ziehl-Neelsen staining. Handle slides in a rack lowered through troughs to ensure uniform treatment between specific and control preparations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complement-fixation (Bordet & Gengou) test setup and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange five test-tubes with defined volumes of complement, test serum (inactivated), control pooled serum, and bacterial antigen; incubate with complement and antigen, then add erythrocyte solution plus haemolysin; absence of haemolysis in test tube indicates presence of specific antibody (complement fixed by antigen–antibody).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reagents: normal saline, erythrocyte solution E, haemolytic serum H.S., complement C, inactivated specific serum S.S., inactivated pooled serum P.S., antigen A. Procedure: into tubes 1–5 pipette complement as directed (0.1 c.c. in tubes 1,3,4,5); add 0.2 c.c. serum to tubes 1 and 2; 0.2 c.c. control serum to tube 4; add 1 c.c. antigen to tubes 1–4; incubate 1 hour at 37°C; then add 1 c.c. erythrocyte solution and four minimal haemolytic doses of haemolysin to each tube, incubate another hour at 37°C, chill 3 hours; interpret: tubes 3–5 should haemolyse; tube 2 should show no haemolysis; tube 1: absence of haemolysis = complement fixed → antibody present; presence of haemolysis = no appreciable antibody. Diagram and controls must be carefully followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional sensitisation of erythrocytes during complement test
rubrics_metrics.description: Erythrocytes may be sensitised shortly before use by incubating erythrocyte solution with haemolysin for 15 minutes at room temperature to prepare 'sensitised' red cells for addition after the first incubation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare 5 c.c. erythrocyte solution + 20 minimal haemolytic doses haemolysin, incubate 15 minutes at room temperature (45 minutes after experiment start), then add 1 c.c. sensitised red cells to tubes at step when tubes are removed after first hour of incubation, proceed with second incubation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perform autopsy promptly and maintain asepsis
rubrics_metrics.description: Carry out post-mortem examination as soon as possible after the animal's death; use searing irons freely and treat instruments as contaminated after use on one structure (use fresh instrument thereafter) to minimise post-mortem contamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: tissues rapidly invaded by bacteria after death. NOTE: "Throughout the autopsy the searing irons must be freely employed, and it must be recollected that one instrument is only to be employed to seize or cut one structure. This done, it must be regarded as contaminated and a fresh instrument taken for the next step." Sterilise instruments by boiling ten minutes before procedure and re-boil infected instruments after use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and setup for necropsy (apparatus and positioning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sterilise instruments by boiling ten minutes; heat searing irons; drench fur/feathers with 2% lysol; fasten body ventral surface upward on board with copper nails (unless otherwise required) and reflect skin using midline incision and transverse cuts to expose cavities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps 1–6: steriliser prep, heat searing irons separately, drench fur to prevent hairs entering cavities and to kill vermin, examine cadaver for non-infectious causes of death, secure body on board by copper nails; incise midline from sternum to pubes and make lateral incisions to reflect skin in flaps. Place infected instruments separately on board or knife rest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site-specific sampling and culture technique during autopsy
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect sterile samples from seat of inoculation, lymph nodes, pleural/pericardial/peritoneal fluids, heart blood, urine, bile, spleen, liver, lungs, kidneys, lymphatic glands, bone marrow and cerebro-spinal fluid for cultivation and microscopic preparations, using searing and sterile instruments and appropriate containers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: sear local lesion and remove deeper material for tube and surface plate cultivations and cover-slip preparations; collect pleuritic/pericardial/peritoneal fluid in pipettes; plunge capillary pipette through seared area of heart ventricle to fill with blood for culture and cover-slip prep; excise spleen and use spear-headed spatula or dab cut surface onto surface plates; for bone marrow, dissect long bones and prepare marrow films by Price-Jones method (dissociating fluid: 10% glycerine neutralised to pH). Ensure each organ’s specimen is placed in separate sterile capsule or bottle with fixing fluid if for sectioning, and label containers fully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cranial and spinal cavity sampling and techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: When required (e.g., rabies), examine cranial cavity and remove brain and spinal cord by reversing the animal and making incisions to reflect skin and dissect muscles, then cut transverse processes and remove vault of skull or use surgical engine with small circular saw to remove skull vault and spinous processes for nervous tissue removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps 29–33: return viscera to abdominal cavity, secure body dorsum-up, incise longitudinal and transverse lines to reflect skin, dissect muscles, cut transverse processes with bone forceps, remove skull vault and spinal processes to expose brain and cord; collect cerebro-spinal fluid for cultures. If using surgical engine, fit small circular saw to expedite and reduce tissue injury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of bone marrow films (Price-Jones method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract marrow by squeezing bone, receive marrow in platinum loop, transfer to dissociating fluid (neutral 10% glycerine prepared and neutralised to pH), place loopful of desiccating fluid and marrow emulsion on slide, spread gently, air dry, stain with Jenner's polychrome for 2.5 minutes, wash, dry and mount in xylol balsam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare dissociating fluid: 10 c.c. Price's glycerine + 90 c.c. sterile ammonia-free distilled water; titrate against n/10 sodic hydrate using phenolphthalein and neutralise. Use gentle spreading to avoid artifact; allow drying protected from dust; staining and mounting per directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling, disposal, and preservation post-autopsy
rubrics_metrics.description: After autopsy, gather infected instruments for sterilisation, sprinkle dry sawdust in cavities to absorb fluids, cover body with blotting/paper moistened with 2% lysol, place in galvanised pail with lid for transport to crematorium, and cremation together with board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps 35–37: return contaminated instruments to steriliser and disinfect by boiling 10 minutes; absorb fluids with dry sawdust; moisten cover paper with 2% lysol; place in pail with lid ready for cremation; cremate cadaver with the board to prevent environmental contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-mortem recording and correlation of findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Make full notes immediately after autopsy of body cavities and viscera; later add results of microscopic and cultural investigations and summarise observations under tissue changes (local and general) and symptoms (associated or without known tissue changes) using a standard autopsy card.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use printed autopsy card (fields: date, animal, number, weight, times of death and autopsy, sections for seat of inoculation, thoracic, abdominal, cranial cavities, bacteriological and histological examinations, organs preserved). Correlate organism isolation results with ante-mortem symptoms. Use schematic figure on reverse for lesion localization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of permanent museum specimens (tissues)
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove tissue/organ promptly, place in wide-mouthed stoppered jar on cotton-wool pad arranged in intended display position, fix in Kaiserling solution for 48 hours–7 days, then transfer through methylated spirit until natural colours restore, then transfer to mounting solution (Jore's or Frost's) and seal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kaiserling modified solution: potassium acetate 30 g, potassium nitrate 15 g in 1000 c.c. distilled water + formalin 150 c.c.; filter and fix tissue 48 hours–7 days; transfer to methylated spirit (95%) 30–60 minutes then fresh spirit until natural colours recovered (3–6 hours average), dry cut surfaces, transfer to Jore's mounting (glycerine 500 c.c., distilled water 750 c.c., formalin 2 c.c.) for 24 hours or until tissue sinks, then place in museum jar with fresh mounting solution and seal. Alternative: fill jar with liquefied gelatine +1% formalin, allow set and seal. Note: Kaiserling solution can be reused if clear; filter if turbidity develops.
